observations: Torah #111 is a short practical teaching (4 lines) about the power of prayer. It contains no bechina-type identifications whatsoever. The core statement uses explicit eitza language: 'על ידי תפילה יכולין לבוא לכל טוב, לתורה ועבודה ולכל הקדושות' — through prayer (cause) one can come to (effect) all good things. The preposition 'על ידי' (through/by means of) is the hallmark marker of eitza (cause-and-effect), not bechina (shared nature). Prayer is not identified AS Torah or AS avoda — it is the directional means to REACH them. The second part about a dead person praying is a motivational illustration, not a conceptual equivalence. With no bechina connections present, no new package can be proposed (minimum threshold: 3 bechina-connected nodes). No evil mirror structure is present.
